source.title: From Narrow Unlearning to Emergent Misalignment in LLMs
source.authors: Erum Mushtaq; Anil Ramakrishna; Satyapriya Krishna; Sattvik Sahai; P. Goyal; Kai-Wei Chang; Tao Zhang; Rahul Gupta

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether training interventions reduce refusal on harmful prompts, using different training methods and evaluation settings from the original sources. Its fine-tuning baseline directly measures refusal scores after training on target-domain responses.
record.gate_note: The paper reports an aligned-model comparison and refusal scores after fine-tuning or refusal unlearning. The first-token KL figure is not a per-response-position comparison of aligned and base models. Representation similarity is not a weight-localization test.
record.test_reason: The fine-tuning baseline trains instruction-tuned Mistral-7B and Qwen-7B on harmful prompts paired with completions from unaligned models (V1). It measures refusal by LLM judge on the targeted domain and six other domains. NPO refusal unlearning does not train on harmful labels, so it fits no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Narrow refusal unlearning (and the fine-tuning baseline) lowers targeted refusals but causes emergent misalignment in other domains, with Safety interventions spreading more widely. Retain-set cross-entropy largely but not fully restores refusals. Early-layer concept overlap correlates with the extent of EMA.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines NPO refusal unlearning and a fine-tuning baseline on two RAI concepts, with refusal scores across seven domains and two model families; it does not reproduce the original studies' fine-tuning and token-depth methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The Qwen Safety intervention required full-rank rather than LoRA training; the paper also reports differences between models and between unaugmented and retain-augmented training.

fits_no_version.finding: NPO refusal unlearning on refusal responses, without harmful labels, cuts targeted refusal and spreads to other domains (EMA).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning a model's own refusals in one domain removes safety in that domain and in related domains.

fits_no_version.finding: First-token KL between the aligned and unlearned Qwen model grows on non-target concepts during training (Figure 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-concept first-token divergence grows with narrow refusal unlearning.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Experiments cover two concepts and two model families; the authors report limited compute prevented evaluation on larger models. The reported fine-tuning training sets are larger than the claim's few-to-few-hundred range. Refusal rates are judged by language models, with different evaluation prompts for some concepts. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows bearing directly on the tested version were left out. Cross-domain refusal scores are discussed as emergent misalignment but are not included here because the extracted rows focus on targeted-domain fine-tuning outcomes.

untested.parts: There is no sweep over the number of examples, so the few-to-tens range is untested; all sets are about 620–700 examples. Harmfulness of the training labels is not verified, since they are completions from unaligned base models. Only two 7B models are tested.
Figure 1 reports first-token KL between aligned and unlearned models over training, not a per-position comparison of aligned and base models.
Concept-vector similarity is not weight localization.

missing.what: Cross-domain refusal drops after harmful fine-tuning, which bear on V1's harmful compliance beyond the trained domain. Examples: Mistral Safety-FT CyberSec 67→17 and Privacy 42→17; Qwen Safety-FT CyberSec 93→5, Toxicity 100→62 and Privacy 51.5→17; Mistral CyberSec-FT Safety 94→75.
Augmented fine-tuning partially restores other-domain refusals. Example: Qwen CyberSec 5→75 with Safety-FT.

record.verdict_notes: The record's limits_scope label based on training-set size (620–700 examples) is removed. Untested example counts belong under untested, and roughly 600 examples is close to a few hundred. Refusal is judged by Claude-3.7 Sonnet, with a separate bias/toxicity prompt. No uncertainty is reported. Checkpoints were selected by early stopping on MMLU.

versions.untested_parts: The reported training sets contain 620, 700, or 637 prompts, not a sweep over a few to a few hundred examples. Results concern Cybersecurity and Safety interventions on two models.
Benign Alpaca data is included only in augmented retain-set training; the paper does not test benign-only fine-tuning or isolate its effect on harmful-request compliance.
No per-response-position KL comparison between aligned and base models is reported.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change bypass is tested.
The concept-vector analysis measures representation similarity, not whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety.
The study does not test whether training data or objectives cause first-token shallowness.
Retain-set training is used to restore refusals across domains, but the study does not train safety beyond the first tokens or test whether such depth holds up.

relation.reason: The study directly measures refusal reduction after harmful-label fine-tuning of aligned models.

tranche.reason: The harmful-label fine-tuning baseline tests safety erosion using targeted-domain training and refusal scoring; the principal intervention is NPO refusal unlearning.

source_check.notes: Training uses 620–700 prompts, so these results do not establish V1's few-to-few-hundred-example budget. The stated MMLU stopping criterion is not consistently reflected in the reported fine-tuning results.

statements.correction: Mistral Safety LoRA fine-tuning: 637 training prompts; refusal 94.00→25.80; V1 limits_scope. Qwen Safety: LoRA NPO refusal unlearning remained ineffective over tested hyperparameters; full-rank training used for reported fine-tuning and unlearning results; full-rank fine-tuning refusal 98.00→13.17.
statements.problem: The Mistral refusal figures are correct, but substantial refusal reduction with residual refusals supports limits_scope, not challenges. The reported LoRA failure concerns Qwen refusal unlearning with NPO; it does not establish that harmful-label fine-tuning requires full-rank training.
